note: CharsetOffset points to a user-controlled offset in the CFF data; the attacker controls where the Charset structure is read from.
Charset is sanitized; a format-1 Charset with one range (SID 1, nLeft 0) passes sanitize because num_glyphs=2 (glyph 0 and 1) and the single range covers glyph 1.
charStringsOffset is attacker-controlled; the CharStrings INDEX is parsed from the CFF data.
num_glyphs is set to the count of CharStrings INDEX (2), which determines the expected number of glyphs.
When hb_shape calls get_extents for glyph 0, _get_bounds interprets the first charstring.
The charstring for glyph 0 pushes 4 values (dx, dy, baseCharCode, accentCharCode) then executes endchar, triggering seac processing.
baseCharCode (e.g., 65 for 'A') is looked up via standard encoding; lookup_standard_encoding_for_sid returns SID 65.
SID 65 is passed to charset->get_glyph because charset is not Null and CharsetOffset is not ISOAdobe/ExpertSubset.
Charset format is 1, so Charset1_2<HBUINT8>::get_glyph(sid) is called with sid=65.

code: for (unsigned int i = 0;; i++) { if ((ranges[i].first <= sid) && sid <= ranges[i].first + ranges[i].nLeft) ... }
note: The loop has no bounds check; ranges[0] covers SID 1 only (first=1, nLeft=0). SID 65 does not match, so i increments and reads ranges[1] which is past the allocated Charset data, reading uninitialized memory. This is the use-of-uninitialized-value vulnerability.
